---
title: "Ex2 - Getting and Knowing your Data (Chipotle) - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

This time we are going to pull data directly from the internet.
Special thanks to: https://github.com/justmarkham for sharing the dataset and materials.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/chipotle.tsv).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called chipo.

```{r}
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/chipotle.tsv"

# the file uses the text "NULL" for missing values in choice_description
chipo <- read_tsv(url, na = c("", "NA", "NULL"))
```

### Step 4. See the first 10 entries

```{r}
head(chipo, 10)
```

### Step 5. What is the number of observations in the dataset?

```{r}
# Solution 1
nrow(chipo)

# Solution 2
glimpse(chipo) # Rows: 4,622
```

### Step 6. What is the number of columns in the dataset?

```{r}
ncol(chipo)
```

### Step 7. Print the name of all the columns.

```{r}
names(chipo)
```

### Step 8. How is the dataset indexed?

```{r}
# tibbles have no index (row labels): rows are identified by their position, 1 to n
seq_len(nrow(chipo)) |> range()
```

### Step 9. Which was the most-ordered item?

```{r}
chipo |>
  group_by(item_name) |>
  summarise(quantity = sum(quantity)) |>
  arrange(desc(quantity)) |>
  head(1)
```

### Step 10. For the most-ordered item, how many items were ordered?

```{r}
# count() with wt = quantity is a shortcut for group_by() + summarise(sum())
chipo |>
  count(item_name, wt = quantity, name = "quantity", sort = TRUE) |>
  head(1)
```

### Step 11. What was the most ordered item in the choice_description column?

```{r}
chipo |>
  filter(!is.na(choice_description)) |>
  count(choice_description, wt = quantity, name = "quantity", sort = TRUE) |>
  head(1)
# Diet Coke 159
```

### Step 12. How many items were orderd in total?

```{r}
total_items_orders <- sum(chipo$quantity)
total_items_orders
```

### Step 13. Turn the item price into a float

#### Step 13.a. Check the item price type

```{r}
class(chipo$item_price)
```

#### Step 13.b. Create a lambda function and change the type of item price

```{r}
# \(x) is R's short syntax for an anonymous (lambda) function
dollarizer <- \(x) as.numeric(str_remove(x, fixed("$")))

chipo <- chipo |> mutate(item_price = dollarizer(item_price))
```

#### Step 13.c. Check the item price type

```{r}
class(chipo$item_price)
```

### Step 14. How much was the revenue for the period in the dataset?

```{r}
revenue <- sum(chipo$quantity * chipo$item_price)

cat("Revenue was: $", round(revenue, 2), "\n", sep = "")
```

### Step 15. How many orders were made in the period?

```{r}
orders <- n_distinct(chipo$order_id)
orders
```

### Step 16. What is the average revenue amount per order?

```{r}
# Solution 1
chipo <- chipo |> mutate(revenue = quantity * item_price)

order_grouped <- chipo |>
  group_by(order_id) |>
  summarise(revenue = sum(revenue))

mean(order_grouped$revenue)

# Solution 2
chipo |>
  summarise(revenue = sum(revenue), .by = order_id) |>
  pull(revenue) |>
  mean()
```

### Step 17. How many different items are sold?

```{r}
n_distinct(chipo$item_name)
```
